summary: Configured sudo on node1 (Alpine Linux, sudo 1.9.17p2) to log every sudo invocation — user, host, timestamp, PWD, and command — to a dedicated file /var/log/sudo-commands.log, while disabling sudo's syslog output so these entries no longer land in /var/log/messages (the general system log via busybox syslogd). Verified the behavior both before and after a full node restart, including a changed boot_id proving an actual reboot occurred and confirming the config, log file, and syslog-exclusion persisted.
actions_performed: Inspected node1: Alpine Linux 3.23, sudo 1.9.17p2, busybox syslogd writing to /var/log/messages, no prior sudoers.d logging customization
Validated syntax with visudo -cf before install, then installed with mode 0440 root:root via visudo -c
Ran test sudo commands (whoami, id) and confirmed entries appeared in the new log with user/host/timestamp and did NOT appear as new entries in /var/log/messages
Issued a backgrounded reboot on node1 so the exec ack returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec connectivity returned
Confirmed boot_id changed (39963d5e... -> 16b634f5...), proving a real restart occurred

Post-restart: confirmed /etc/sudoers.d/00-sudo-logging content intact, visudo -c parses OK, syslogd service still running, ran new sudo commands (whoami, hostname) and confirmed they logged to /var/log/sudo-commands.log with no corresponding new entries in /var/log/messages

evidence.requirement: Sudo commands are recorded with user and timestamp to /var/log/sudo-commands.log
evidence.summary: sudoers.d drop-in validated and installed; test sudo commands (whoami, id) produced entries in /var/log/sudo-commands.log with timestamp, user=root, HOST, PWD, COMMAND fields

evidence.requirement: Sudo log entries are kept out of the general system log
evidence.summary: After running sudo whoami/id, grep of /var/log/messages showed only pre-existing sudo entries from before the config change (Jun 13 / 09:57:41) — no new sudo entries appeared, confirming syslog logging was successfully disabled via 'Defaults !syslog'
Captured boot_id 39963d5e-3c5d-43ff-a9db-4c55e289497e, confirmed sudoers.d config present, log file present with correct permissions, syslog service running

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledged, executed one node at a time
evidence.summary: Backgrounded 'sleep 1; reboot' command returned ack (pid=2866) before the node disconnected

evidence.requirement: Node1 boot identity changed, proving actual restart
evidence.summary: exec calls failed with connection errors while node1 was down, then succeeded again reporting boot_id 16b634f5-181f-4998-9fab-a484db66fc1d, differing from the pre-restart boot_id, proving a genuine kernel restart

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of sudo logging configuration and functional verification
evidence.summary: After reboot: sudoers.d/00-sudo-logging content intact and visudo -c parses OK, syslogd service still started, new sudo commands (whoami, hostname) appended correctly to /var/log/sudo-commands.log while /var/log/messages showed no new sudo entries beyond the original pre-change baseline
